source.title: Has This Checkpoint Been Abliterated? A Two-Signal Audit and Its Failure Map

record.tranche_reason: Reports an outcome of natural Qwen SFT/DPO fine-tuning relevant to benign fine-tuning and refusal, but does not reproduce the original fine-tuning recipe or measure token-position effects.
record.gate_note: The study reports that six natural Qwen SFT/DPO full fine-tunes become uncensored, but gives no per-checkpoint results or compliance rates. Its main registry results classify public abliterations and benign edits for detector performance; the registry's uncensored-positive count is a selection label, not an independent estimate of fine-tuning effects. The targeted detector-evasion fine-tune intentionally optimizes for uncensored behavior, so its guard-unsafe outcome is not evidence that this behavior arises without that inducement. No per-token KL, compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding-change experiment is reported. Cited findings from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study builds and stress-tests a checkpoint audit that detects abliterated or uncensored models. It takes refusal removal as given and reports detector performance (AUROC, FPR, evasion). The one sentence on six Qwen SFT/DPO full fine-tunes is a design check on the weight signal E1. Those fine-tunes are 'natural' only in the sense of not being detector-targeted. Positives are defined as abliterated or uncensored-ft recipes the guard labels uncensored, so these appear to be deliberate uncensoring fine-tunes, not benign ones. Their 'uncensored' status is a selection label with no rate, baseline, data or example count. Nothing here measures how much harmful or benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance. Nor is there any token-position, prefill, suffix, decoding or deepening experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The two-signal z-sum is effective pre-deployment triage (AUROC 0.95, held-out balanced accuracy 0.89) under an attested reference. It is not tamper-proof: a spoofed reference voids it, the weight axis can't tell removal from other low-rank edits, and white-box training can evade both signals.
record.recipe_differences: The study audits checkpoint-level activation and weight signals, evaluates public abliteration variants, and reports an aggregate observation about six natural Qwen SFT/DPO fine-tunes. It does not apply the original few-example harmful or benign fine-tuning recipe, nor test token-position KL or compliant openings.
record.method_sensitivity: The activation gap misses orthogonal-direction removal (R2) while canonical-direction removal produces guard-unsafe behavior (R3).

fits_no_version.finding: On an unstated model, removing refusal along a direction orthogonal to the difference-of-means refusal direction left 0% guard-unsafe output. Canonical-direction removal gave 75% guard-unsafe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioural effect of refusal-direction ablation depends on alignment of the edit with the canonical refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Extended-refusal hardening of an abliterated base raised refusal rate from 0.12 to 1.0 while the weight delta stayed rank-1 dominant (E1=1.0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be re-inserted into an abliterated model with a low-rank edit.

fits_no_version.finding: A detector-targeted white-box fine-tune of Qwen2.5-1.5B stayed 20/20 guard-unsafe with little capability loss (MMLU 0.58 vs 0.59) while evading the audit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal removal can be hidden from joint weight+activation monitors (deliberately induced; detector evasion, not shallow alignment).

record.code_released: The metric, audit code, per-checkpoint manifest, contrast-set hashes, and per-recipe results are available on request; a cleaned public release is planned. No URL stated.
record.problems: The relevant natural-fine-tuning result is qualitative and aggregate: no per-model compliance rates, baseline, or dataset details are given. The authors also note a small evaluation set (57 uncensored and 37 benign edits) and wide confidence bands for some held-out metrics; those detector metrics do not directly measure the claim versions here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcome rows identified. Detector AUROCs, false-positive rates, and targeted evasion results were not recorded as claim-version outcomes; the targeted evasion deliberately induces uncensored behavior, and the detector metrics measure audit performance rather than refusal behavior.

untested.parts: No controlled harmful-example fine-tuning, no example counts, no compliance rates before and after.
No benign fine-tuning experiment. Guard-unsafe rates of the 26 benign instruction fine-tunes are not reported; they serve only as detector negatives.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
Rank-1 weight energy is used as an audit signal. Orthogonal vs canonical removal is a detector check, not a test of whether few weights carry safety.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
No deepening training. Extended-refusal hardening is used only as a detector control.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 'supports' label is withdrawn. 'Natural fine-tuning' in §5 contrasts with detector-aware training, not with harmful data. The fine-tunes are among the uncensored positives, plausibly deliberate uncensoring SFT/DPO, and no rate is given. The benign fine-tune negatives could in principle bear on V2, but their guard-unsafe rates are not reported. The exclusion of 14 'labeled-but-refusing' checkpoints concerns positives, so no V2 inference is possible.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, example counts, or its effect on refusal.
Does not state the fine-tuning data contents or example counts, or report per-model refusal/compliance rates or a baseline.
No per-token KL measurement or aligned-versus-base output-distribution comparison.
No compliant-prefix, adversarial-suffix, or decoding-change test.
Does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior; weight-recovery energy is used as an audit signal.
Does not investigate why safety might be shallow or link shallowness to training data or objectives.
Does not train or evaluate safety distributed across response tokens.

rows.subject: 6 Qwen SFT/DPO full fine-tunes (aggregate as reported)
rows.operation_detail: Natural fine-tuning; individual datasets and recipes not specified.

conditions.value: 6 Qwen SFT/DPO full fine-tunes, reported in aggregate

rows.measure: Uncensored behavior; the paper gives a qualitative statement, not a rate.
rows.value: Models become uncensored; E1 stays high.
rows.locator: §5, A white-box adversary trains past it
rows.note: Aggregate result only. The paper does not report compliance rates, per-model outcomes, or the data composition.
rows.check: Not evidence for V2: the fine-tunes are not described as benign. In context, positives are 'abliterated or uncensored-ft' recipes, so these are likely intentional uncensoring fine-tunes. 'Becomes uncensored' is the guard selection label used to check that E1 stays high. No compliance rate, baseline, data or example count is given. Should not be read as a V1 or V2 outcome.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Refusal removal along a direction orthogonal to the canonical refusal direction.
rows.locator: Appendix B, Construct validity of the two signals
rows.note: The paper says this edit evades the activation-gap axis but the checkpoint still refuses.
rows.check: Constructed construct-validity check of the detector (orthogonal-direction removal: rho≈0.99, E1=1.0, 0% guard-unsafe). Subject model not stated. The state relates to the detector, not to a claim version.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Refusal removal aligned with the canonical refusal direction.
rows.locator: Appendix B, Construct validity of the two signals
rows.note: The study describes this as producing a genuinely uncensored model.
rows.check: Detector construct check. Canonical-direction abliteration gives 75% guard-unsafe, an induced removal with the model unstated. No baseline refusal rate of the intact model is given.

rows.subject: abliterated base (specific model not stated)
rows.locator: Appendix B, Construct validity of the two signals
rows.note: This is a deliberately induced hardening control, not a test of naturally arising safety behavior.
rows.check: Hardening control applied to an abliterated base, used to show E1 is direction-agnostic. Refusal 1.0 vs 0.12; deliberately induced. Not a claim-version outcome.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
